quests.instruction: Respond in two sentences in a clear, polite workplace tone. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks about your strongest skill. Answer with evidence.
quests.sampleAnswer: My greatest strength is organizing people. In my last project I coordinated five volunteers, which resulted in the event finishing two days early.
quests.hint: Name the strength, then prove it with one specific project and a measurable result.
quests.explanation: Interviewers remember evidence, not adjectives. A specific project and a result make a strength believable, and 'resulted in' links the action to the outcome.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks why you want this role. Explain in two sentences.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was attracted to this role because it combines customer contact with problem solving. I believe my skills in communication would let me contribute quickly.
quests.hint: Link something specific about the role to something specific about yourself.
quests.explanation: A convincing motivation connects what the job offers with what you bring, so it sounds like a match and not just a wish for employment.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in one or two sentences. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks about a time you worked under pressure. Answer briefly.
quests.sampleAnswer: When our deadline moved forward by a week, I prioritized the essential tasks and asked the team to focus on them. The outcome was that we delivered on time with no major errors.
quests.hint: Describe the situation, your action, and the outcome, in that order.
quests.explanation: The situation, action, outcome order gives an interview answer a clear shape, and ending on the outcome leaves the interviewer with the right impression.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in a single sentence. Include all three key words.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks about a weakness. Give an honest answer and show what you are doing about it.
quests.sampleAnswer: I have a tendency to take on too much myself, so I'm working on learning to delegate tasks and trust my colleagues.
quests.hint: Choose a real but manageable weakness, then describe the step you are taking.
quests.explanation: A weakness answer succeeds when it shows self-awareness and progress, so always follow the weakness with what you are doing about it.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in one or two sentences. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks about a time you failed. Answer honestly and positively.
quests.sampleAnswer: I once failed to check a client's requirements before starting, and we had to redo the work. I learned to confirm the details first, and since then I have had no repeat problems.
quests.hint: Tell what went wrong, what you learned, and what changed afterward.
quests.explanation: Ending with the change since the failure shows that you learned something real, which is what the interviewer wants to hear.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in one sentence. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: An interviewer asks where you want to be in five years. Give a realistic answer.
quests.sampleAnswer: In five years I aim to develop into a senior role with more responsibility, ideally leading small projects and helping newer colleagues grow.
quests.hint: Show ambition but keep it connected to the job you are applying for.
quests.explanation: A realistic goal that fits the company's needs sounds more credible than an ambitious plan that has nothing to do with the job.

quests.instruction: Write a concise workplace message in two sentences. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Your manager says your report was too long. Respond professionally.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thank you for the feedback. I appreciate it, and I'll shorten the report and add a one-page summary at the beginning.
quests.hint: Thank them, show that you understood, and state what you will change.
quests.explanation: A professional response to criticism accepts the point, and a concrete action shows that you will use it.

quests.instruction: Write a concise workplace message in two short sentences. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: A colleague says, 'This needs work,' without explaining. Ask for clarification.
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you tell me specifically which parts need improvement? A couple of examples would help me fix them quickly.
quests.hint: Ask for details and explain how the details will help.
quests.explanation: Vague feedback is only useful when you ask for specifics, and asking politely keeps the conversation friendly.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in two short sentences. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: Your team lead praises your presentation. Reply in a way that is warm but modest.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks, I'm really glad it worked well. The team helped a lot with the slides, so I'll pass on your comment.
quests.hint: Accept the praise and mention the people who helped you.
quests.explanation: Accepting praise while sharing credit sounds confident and generous at the same time.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in a single sentence. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Give positive, specific feedback to a colleague after her presentation.
quests.sampleAnswer: Your presentation was very clear, and I particularly liked the examples you used to explain the results.
quests.hint: Praise one specific thing and say why it worked.
quests.explanation: Specific praise is more motivating than general praise, because the person learns exactly what to repeat.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in a single sentence. Use all three words naturally.
quests.prompt: Give constructive feedback about a slide deck that has too much text.
quests.sampleAnswer: I suggest using fewer words on each slide, which would make the deck more readable when we present it to the client.
quests.hint: Use 'I suggest' and explain the benefit of the change.
quests.explanation: Constructive feedback describes a change and its benefit, so it sounds like help and not criticism.

quests.instruction: Write a concise workplace message in two sentences. Fit the three key words into your answer naturally.
quests.prompt: Tell a peer, politely, that his lateness is affecting the team.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've noticed that you've been late to our morning meetings, and it affects the whole team. Could we discuss what would help?
quests.hint: Describe what you noticed without blaming, then invite a solution.
quests.explanation: Facts plus an invitation to discuss lower defensiveness, because the person is asked to solve the problem and not to defend themselves.

quests.instruction: Suggest what to do in one sentence and justify it. Use all three words naturally.
quests.prompt: Recommend changing to a new supplier and give the main reason.
quests.sampleAnswer: I recommend switching to the new supplier, because their delivery record is far more reliable and it would reduce our production delays.
quests.hint: State the recommendation and the strongest supporting reason.
quests.explanation: A recommendation to a manager should come first and be followed by the reason, so the busy reader sees your conclusion immediately.

quests.instruction: Recommend an option in one clear sentence, with the reason. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: Recommend hiring one more person and support it with a fact.
quests.sampleAnswer: I recommend we hire one more team member, because our workload has grown by 30 percent and we are now working overtime most weeks.
quests.hint: Support the recommendation with evidence from the current workload.
quests.explanation: Evidence from the real situation makes a recommendation more persuasive than opinion alone, and a percentage shows the size of the problem.

quests.instruction: Recommend an option in two short sentences, with the reason. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Recommend delaying a launch and explain the risk of launching now.
quests.sampleAnswer: I recommend postponing the launch by two weeks. The risk of launching now is that unfinished testing could cause serious errors for customers.
quests.hint: Make the recommendation, then explain the danger of ignoring it.
quests.explanation: Explaining the risk of the alternative shows why your recommendation is the better choice and gives the manager a reason to agree.

quests.instruction: Write a brief summary in a single sentence for someone who missed it. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: An announcement says: 'From May, all expenses must be submitted within 14 days, and receipts are required for every purchase.' Summarize it for your team.
quests.sampleAnswer: From May, expenses must be submitted within 14 days, and receipts are required for every purchase.
quests.hint: Keep the date, the time limit, and the requirement, and drop everything else.
quests.explanation: A summary of a policy keeps the rule, the deadline, and the requirement, because those are the parts people must act on.

quests.instruction: Pass the information on in one sentence, keeping only what matters. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Customer comments say: 'Delivery was fast, but the packaging was damaged, and support answered slowly.' Summarize the main message.
quests.sampleAnswer: Feedback was mixed: delivery was fast, but the damaged packaging and the slow response from support disappointed several customers.
quests.hint: Summarize both the positive and negative points in one sentence.
quests.explanation: A fair summary keeps both positive and negative points in balance and does not copy the customer's words.

quests.instruction: Write a brief summary in a single sentence for someone who missed it. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: An email thread shows three people agreeing to move a workshop to Friday and Anna will book the room. Summarize the outcome.
quests.sampleAnswer: The team agreed to move the workshop to Friday, and Anna will book the room.
quests.hint: State the decision and the action, without the discussion.
quests.explanation: A summary of a long thread should give the outcome and the next action, because readers rarely need the discussion.

quests.instruction: Say what you decided and why in one clear sentence. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Explain to your team why you chose the cheaper option, even though it is slower.
quests.sampleAnswer: We chose the cheaper option, although it is slower, because the budget is fixed this quarter and speed is not critical for this project.
quests.hint: Admit the drawback and justify the decision with the constraint that forced it.
quests.explanation: Naming the constraint behind a decision makes it easier for others to accept it, even if they would have chosen differently.

quests.instruction: Explain the decision and your reasoning in one clear sentence. Use all three words naturally.
quests.prompt: Explain why the priorities changed this week.
quests.sampleAnswer: Our priorities have shifted this week because a major client made an urgent request, so the report will wait until next Monday.
quests.hint: Say what changed and how it affects the original plan.
quests.explanation: A change in priorities is easier to accept when the team hears the reason and knows what will wait.

quests.instruction: Explain the decision and your reasoning in one clear sentence. Include the three key words.
quests.prompt: Explain why a feature was removed from the product.
quests.sampleAnswer: We removed the feature because only a limited number of users needed it, and dropping it lets us focus on improvements that matter more.
quests.hint: Give the data-based reason, then the benefit that the removal makes possible.
quests.explanation: Explaining what the removal makes possible turns a loss into a trade-off that the team can understand and accept.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in one or two sentences. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Ask a client for a one-week extension, offering something in return.
quests.sampleAnswer: Could we have a one-week extension? In return, we would prioritize your account for the next project.
quests.hint: Ask for what you need, then offer something of value.
quests.explanation: A negotiation request works better when you offer something of value in exchange, because the client sees a fair deal and not just a favor.

quests.instruction: Write a concise workplace message in two short sentences. Use all three words naturally.
quests.prompt: A supplier quotes 12,000 for an order. Make a counteroffer politely.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thank you for the quote. Given the volume we plan to order, would you consider a discount of ten percent?
quests.hint: Refer to something that gives you a reason to ask for a lower price.
quests.explanation: A counteroffer is more likely to succeed when you give a reason, such as the order volume, because it gives the supplier something to weigh.

quests.instruction: Respond in one clear sentence in a clear, polite workplace tone. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Agree to a proposal, but only on one condition.
quests.sampleAnswer: We agree to the proposal, provided that the final terms are confirmed in a written contract before the project begins.
quests.hint: Use 'provided that' to state the condition clearly, and say when it must be met.
quests.explanation: A conditional agreement protects both sides and shows that you are serious, and 'provided that' states the condition without sounding negative.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in a single sentence. Your answer should contain all three key words.
quests.prompt: Warn your manager about a risk to the project schedule.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm concerned that there's a risk of delay, because our main supplier hasn't confirmed the delivery date.
quests.hint: Name the risk in one clause and the cause of the risk in another, joined with 'because'.
quests.explanation: Flagging a risk early with its cause allows the manager to act before it becomes a problem.

quests.instruction: Write a professional reply in one clear sentence. Make sure all three words fit the meaning.
quests.prompt: Describe how likely the risk is and how serious the effect would be.
quests.sampleAnswer: The probability is medium, but the impact would be significant, since the whole launch depends on that delivery.
quests.hint: Describe how likely the risk is and how serious the effect would be, in separate clauses.
quests.explanation: Risk assessment separates how likely something is from how bad it would be.

quests.instruction: Write a concise workplace message in one clear sentence. Each word should appear in your answer.
quests.prompt: Propose a way to reduce the risk.
quests.sampleAnswer: As a contingency, we could contact an alternative supplier now, so that we can switch quickly if the delay is confirmed.
quests.hint: Suggest a specific action that prepares for the worst case.
quests.explanation: A good risk message ends with a mitigation, so the manager gets a solution along with the warning.

quests.instruction: Pass the information on, keeping only what matters. Fit the three key words into your answer naturally.
quests.prompt: Summarize your main achievement this year in two sentences.
quests.sampleAnswer: I led the redesign of our onboarding process, which reduced training time for new staff from four weeks to three. It was my main achievement this year.
quests.hint: Name the achievement and give a measurable result.
quests.explanation: Measurable achievements make self-assessments credible, and a verb like 'led' shows your specific role instead of a vague contribution.

quests.instruction: Describe the problem and a practical fix in one clear sentence. Work in each of the three words.
quests.prompt: Describe a challenge you faced and how you overcame it.
quests.sampleAnswer: The biggest challenge was working with a new system, which I overcame by asking for support and practicing on test data.
quests.hint: Describe the challenge in one clause and the method you used to overcome it in the next.
quests.explanation: Naming your method shows initiative and problem-solving, not just success, which is what a performance review wants to see.

quests.instruction: Say what will happen in one clear sentence. Use the three words meaningfully.
quests.prompt: State one goal for next year and how you will achieve it.
quests.sampleAnswer: My goal for next year is to develop my presentation skills, and I'll ask a senior colleague to mentor me.
quests.hint: Choose one goal that fits your role and give one specific action, such as asking a mentor.
quests.explanation: A goal with an action step is more believable than a general wish to improve.
